scenes.summary: Lucky Carrot explains the difference between staple goods and elastic goods. Additionally, investing stock bills in other areas will further expand the variety of goods available.

lines.text: Oh? You seem genuinely interested in stock redistribution.
Excellent. In that case, let me walk you through how to further ⟦key|diversify our supplies⟧.
I do! But stock bills aren't the main issue right now.
Of course not. If anything, we're about to do some real good.
We've got a messy situation right now. Many areas still haven't reestablished contact.
If you can reconnect those areas and give me more stock bills, I'll restore the full supply network and diversify our inventory.
Also, given conditions on the ground, our managed supplies fall into two categories: staple goods and elastic goods.
Since supply and demand fluctuate constantly, ⟦key|elastic goods⟧ always have volatile pricing — which also presents an opportunity.
Naturally, though it'll still be handled through stock bills. Any proceeds will ultimately flow back into the local economy.
After all, this is a risk-mitigation mechanism endorsed by the Band Accord. Meeting urgent needs where they arise, for mutual benefit.
I'll also monitor regional operations and set transaction limits on elastic goods to prevent excessive impact.
Reconnect the areas, upgrade the stock redistribution system, expand its reach, and keep an eye on elastic ⟦key|market trends⟧. That's the plan.
Someday we'll manage supplies across even more areas. For now, let's give it our all here in Valley IV!

options: You're not asking me to do anything shady, are you?
So you really are an expert in this field...
Keep up the good work. I'll rely on your oversight.
